Female Wardens

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Working at South Africa's most dangerous prisons, female wardens have repeatedly alleged abuse and neglect. This episode explores challenges faced by female wardens.

Unique Selling Point:
Although it has gotten easier to survive in a male dominated culture, challenges still face women in corrections. South Africans hardly hear about the challenges facing women in South African prisons. In this episode we investigate what it would take for the CSD to make major changes in a bid to protect female wardens that work across the country.

Summary:
In August last year, 50 year old Eunice Moloko was found dead in the COVID-19 isolation unit at the Leeuwkop Prison. Her body was found on the floor with her jacket covered in blood. She clocked in for work, alongside her husband (who also happens to work in another section) at 7AM. She never made it home. Her husband knew something was amiss when Eunice didn’t meet him at the car park. He then proceeds to call and investigate her possible whereabouts. After many failed attempts, he got back into the prison and had to burgle his way into the section in which she was believed to be working. He made the shocking discovery of her body. We latter found out that a prisoner who had access to the various units, was responsible for her death. He strangled and raped her. He appeared at the Wynberg court in November last year, tried again for murder.

Her death reveals a lot of what has been bothering other female wardens regarding understaffing and overcrowding. As per security policies, female wardens are supposed to be accompanied by male counterparts at all times. From the information about her death, it is clear tha Eunice was left alone in the isolation unit. This is something that female colleagues complained about especially during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. It was also clear that she did not get security visits throughout the day. She was also not relieved during the expected lunch time. There was also no concern when she had not submitted the ward keys during the expected knock-off time.


Further information:
All of this is happening because of major failings of the department. The biggest issue is overcrowding and understaffing.
The department has about 243 correctional centers, which works out to about 138 070 inmates across SA. Only about 118 070 beds. This means that it’s dealing with an overcrowding rate of more than 20%.

This becomes very difficult for wardens to control prisoners. Over the years POPCRU has noted an increase in fatal altercations. The issue is more pressing with female wardens because they are not protected.

For example, the security policy tha relates to women states that women are supposed to be accompanied at all times by a male colleague. We know that this is not happening. In fact all the women we spoke to that they often get in trouble with management when they ask for an escort. They are told its not practical because they are short staffed.

Press Release:


Working in some of South Africa's notorious male prisons is tough – and for some women, it’s a calling where they hope to make a difference in the lives of inmates who often have nothing
left to lose. But increasingly female wardens, armed with nothing more than tasers and batons, have fallen victim to assault, rape and even killing. Carte Blanche goes behind the gates and walls as the women describe a life of fear, violence and harassment
on the job behind bars.  

Script:


AUDIO
VO - It was August 2021 when colleagues of the late Eunice Moloko gathered outside the Alexandra Magistrates Court for a glimpse of the man accused of killing her.

Moloko’s family was grief-struck, seeing the accused. Thirteen days earlier, the Leeukop prison employee was found in her office - dead. It wasn’t the first time an inmate had raped and killed a female warden in South Africa’s prisons.

Reports of such attacks are chilling for three female wardens who told us they only wanted to make a difference in a male dominated world.
THANDO - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – DAY TWO CLIP #2
03:41 - Wearing that uniform for the first time was a dream come true.


LIZZY JOHANNESBURG PRISON WARDEN - DAY ONE CLIP 00123
When I came from college, when people see me around the township, and people respected me so much.
– JOHANNESBURG PRISON WARDEN - DAY ONE

02:48 - ... I used to wake up happy to go to work, because it’s what I love.
LINK - Most people are happy to find any means to make a living but these women only wanted to be in one profession – that of prison warden. But when they finally put on the uniform, what at first seemed like a dream come true, turned out to be a horrific nightmare and has left them too scared to even show up to work.
VO - Female guards we spoke to believe Eunice Moloko died because the Department of Correctional Services fails to fix systemic problems.

But spokesperson Singabakho Nxumalo says it’s far more complex.
NXUMALO INTERVIEW

Nxumalo - 00:53 the reason why we are saying that is that correctional facilities, when we hear of security breach cases or where there has been an attack or assault. It is really rare where we find that a female official has been attacked.
01:10 and it is rare where that there has been
Busi 01:24 those cases are still there... what do you think is the problem?
01:37 and our investigation pointed out that there was no compliance to our standard operating procedures. 01:59 because our policy is clear - females must be in the company of male officials

LINK - Internal prison policy states that female wardens at facilities where male inmates are incarcerated must at all times be accompanied by a male counterpart. but is this a realistic expectation considering the combined problems of overcrowding and understaffing.

VO – This warden we call Thando, from Goedemoed Prison in the Free State, felt comforted by the “buddy system”.
WARDEN ONE - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – DAY TWO CLIP #2

01:30 Their job is not only to guard the offenders, but to guard us as well. 01:40.
VO – But the buddy system failed her when she needed it the most.

In 2019, an inmate cornered Thando and another female guard. Things got volatile.

VO – The prisoner locked out a male officer from the section in which the two women were working in their respective offices.



WARDEN ONE - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – CLIP #2

02:02 I heard a scream, so loud, that I couldn’t continue with my books. 02:13 I went out to look, I realised that it was a female official. my colleague. 02:17 And this is the offender that left.
02:22 When I tried to intervene. “What is happening???!! Leave her!!! Leave her!!!” 02:27 - The offender let go of her. 02:30 - When I looked at her, her eyes were still open and she wasn’t saying anything.


VO – Bewildered, she ran back to the office but the door was broken and could not lock.
WARDEN ONE - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – CLIP #2

02:41 I hid myself under the desk 02:44 When I looked, his hand was covered with blood and even on his uniform he had blood. 02:52 He said “I want to sleep with you, just once”. 02:55 Then I told him that I won't be able to and to make matters worse I’m pregnant. 03:00 He demanded that I take off my clothes. 03:04 And then he raped me.
(we need a breather here, maybe a second or two to take in the weight of what she just told us)
VO – Her colleague succumbed to injuries from a hammer and a pair of scissors.
LINK - Disheartened that authorities are not sympathetic to their plight, aggrieved wardens roped in a law firm to take their concerns to court. Correctional services officials say victims should be claiming for compensation for injuries sustained at work, while the attorneys argue that there probably wouldn't be any victims had the department provided a safe work environment to begin with.


In Johannesburg, this warden we call Tshidi sees rising attacks on women officers with great concern.


WARDEN THREE – JOHANNESBURG PRISON WARDEN

05:01 We mostly work with people who have raped, killed and have wronged the community in other ways.

12:03 – BUSI - How has this impacted on your mental health?

05:19 - [pauses and cries] sometimes I don’t feel right thinking about how 14:59 - I was once admitted for depression three years ago.
Thando says it’s no better at Goedemoed Prison,
WARDEN ONE - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – CLIP #2

08:32 - ... They will be staring at you. They’ll be whistling like [whistles] 08:47 - They will give you that eye, that “I want to sleep with you right now”.
VO - Thando says female guards generally don’t feel safe at work but won’t speak out for fear of the repercussions.

Nxumalo insists the department has created a safe space for women to report concerns.

Nxumalo 13:10 but there are channels for our staff members to raise...

Busi 13:13 but they are saying those channels are not efficient enough, they have been raising those issues but they aren’t taken up.

Nxumalo - 13:20 but where because even if they feel uncomfortable to raise those issues via those channels where they can even hide their identities.

LINK - The wardens we spoke to say their training did not fully equip them for the task of watching over inmates convicted of heinous crimes, some of whom have nothing to lose as they will be in prison for the rest of their lives.
VO – The inmate accused of ending Eunice Moloko's life had been serving an eighteen-year sentence for murder. The man behind the Goedemoed incident had two life terms for previous crimes, including murder and rape. He received two additional life terms for the prison attack.

This Johannesburg Prison official said her anxiety is heightened by having to share protective equipment with her other colleagues. We call her Sizakele.


WARDEN TWO – JOHANNESBURG PRISON WARDEN – CLIP 00123

Busi – 04:18 - And how do you protect yourself?

04:22 - I protect myself by all means, maybe to not shout at them, to be friendly just to calm them. 15:59 we are usually like mothers to them. When they see us they call us mothers. But at the end of the day, you are a mother today, tomorrow they can attack you. So you need to be careful.

VO – Shockingly, Sizakele relies on her wits to survive a facility packed with criminals.
But Nxumalo says if security measures at prisons are upheld, they’re enough to curb attacks against women. Despite evident gaps, his faith in the buddy system is unshaken.
SINGABAKHO NXUMALO – DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONAL SERVICES

Busi 02:51 We have been speaking to women who work in corrections and that’s one of the major problems that they have highlighted- that sometimes they have to be stationed in positions in offices in places alone without any kind of supervision.

Nxumalo 03:15 that is something that can never be allowed. And why am I saying that - is that all heads of centers and even our own officials know about these standard operating procedures.

04:08 hence then it’s unheard of that female officials could be deployed on their own..

Busi Interrupts 04:14 I’m telling you now that is the reality of some of the women we spoke to.

Nxumalo 04:41 but how truthful is that? The reason I’m asking - you’ve got two way radios that they have signed for. They cannot take their positions without being given proper B equipment. They cannot take their positions if they feel vulnerable. They cannot take their positions wherever there is I mine too danger and they feel their lives are at risk.
05:01 because they’ve got all the rights to say I cannot be deployed in that area being
so vulnerable. And measures have to be taken to ensure that at no point do officials feels in that particular way…

Busi - 08:26 But what are you saying then Mr Nxumalo, are you telling us that they are lying?
Even for male officials they cannot find themselves isolated in a particular section of the facility. Hence the Buddy system

Busi - 08:47 so how is that we have cases like the ones that happened in goedemoed, where it was clear that the victims that were involved were not with a male warden. It may happen. And that’s my point. The rule is there. There might be a willingness to implement the rule but in reality this is not what is happening.

Nxumalo 09:15 we only know of two cases where our standard operating procedures where not followed and the results were fatal. Unfortunately so. Only two cases.


VO - The department is now emphasizing self-defence training for women and has recruited more wardens to ease the workload.

He stresses that an attack on any employee is unfortunate and painful.
WARDEN ONE - GOEDEMOED PRISON WARDEN – CLIP #2

I’m the one suffering more than the one who is deceased because I cannot take away the picture I have of her. 09:42 I still hear her scream. 09:46 Sometimes I jump when someone else is screaming, even if its just kids playing.09:52 That situation traumatised me. It makes me feel so fragile.

After many failed attempts, he got back into the prison and had to burgle his way into the section in which she was believed to be working. He made the shocking discovery of her body. We latter found out that a prisoner who had access to the various units, was responsible for her death. He strangled and raped her. He appeared at the Wynberg court in November last year, tried again for murder. Her death reveals a lot of what has been bothering other female wardens regarding understaffing and overcrowding. As per security policies, female wardens are supposed to be accompanied by male counterparts at all times. From the information about her death, it is clear tha Eunice was left alone in the isolation unit. This is something that female colleagues complained about especially during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. It was also clear that she did not get security visits throughout the day. She was also not relieved during the expected lunch time. There was also no concern when she had not submitted the ward keys during the expected knock-off time.
metadata.Further information: All of this is happening because of major failings of the department. The biggest issue is overcrowding and understaffing. The department has about 243 correctional centers, which works out to about 138 070 inmates across SA. Only about 118 070 beds. This means that it’s dealing with an overcrowding rate of more than 20%. This becomes very difficult for wardens to control prisoners. Over the years POPCRU has noted an increase in fatal altercations. The issue is more pressing with female wardens because they are not protected. For example, the security policy tha relates to women states that women are supposed to be accompanied at all times by a male colleague. We know that this is not happening. In fact all the women we spoke to that they often get in trouble with management when they ask for an escort. They are told its not practical because they are short staffed.
